analysis:
Examined all six units, including file metadata, the Serve patch, BASE startup/registration/attestation flow, and HEAD ModelLoading lines 1044–1689. The only changed executable line fully supplied here is ProviderLoop+Serve.swift HEAD 108: host-service runs select VerifiedWeightHashStore.path() before startup preload. No supplied evidence shows this assignment bypassing authorization, weakening encryption, or exposing prompts or credentials. Existing registration seeds liveModelHashes (BASE 214–217); connection-control handling independently invalidates authorization (BASE 399–426). These controls are unchanged.
ModelLoading excerpts retain unload/drain ownership accounting, activation-reserve floors, cancellation checks, eviction protection, load-error sanitization (1651–1668), and loaded-only hash reporting (1195–1204). Their lines are outside the complete changed ranges, so potential issues in this surrounding behavior are not established PR regressions. Relevant contracts include A-004/T-012/T-027 for weight identity, T-041 for verified cache model bindings, TB-007 for native lifetime/availability, and T-053 for connection authorization; no direct change to attestation, fan authority, billing, or hop encryption appears here.
Integration must examine VerifiedWeightHashStore path/read/write validation and consumers, plus ModelLoading HEAD 542–658 and loadWeightHasher initialization: the bounded orientation patch indicates managed GLM manifest verification replaces earlier hashing, but its implementation is not supplied in these units. Verify that persisted observations cannot substitute for verification of loaded bytes or weaken SSD weightHash bindings. Also reconcile startup ordering: revision monitoring and the local endpoint start before the new store-path assignment (Serve BASE 92–101); whether they can publish hashes before initialization depends on omitted implementations. These are unverified cross-file contracts, not supported vulnerabilities.
